scope: Bounded virtual cursor layout, actual owned-overlay pixels/geometry, idle lifecycle, standalone MCP settings/input, actual Ouroboros menus and profile persistence. This is not a clean-layout or UX-parity assessment.

Four label placements, font8/48, three badge shapes, five badge placements, badge-without-label and maxwide size256 combination render distinct relevant pixel hashes. Idle hides native HWND and status without changing saved visibility or pointer position. Paused idle settles, Resume does not wake; saved visible=false stays hidden after mouse activity.

limits: Virtual IDs, owned disposable x64/x86 targets/files and own HWND/GUI pixels only. No hardware/RustDesk input used for control or validation and no OS input injection. No arbitrary-app, hardware, full functional/UX parity or same-process multi-user isolation claim.

Controller/GUI and overlay windows execute x64; x86 is an owned target. i686 executable is built/copied/hashed and used as probe, not a separately exercised x86 GUI controller. No exhaustive size/font/placement/architecture cross product.

Actual bitmap captures independently establish bounded geometry and changed pixels. The exact512px text-width bound is producer/source coverage; the runner checks scalar/truncation metadata and total native canvas, not an independent glyph-width measurement. No general font/glyph-legibility claim; GUI CJK boxes and dense visual hierarchy remain visible limitations.

Connected-agent activity/authorization path is source/producer coverage only. Standalone MCP Manual, replay and replica activity is independently exercised. No extra Agent Access or historical feature suite replay.

Owned HWND PrintWindow observes the actual cached rendering; screen composition, DPI/monitor Cartesian coverage, forced native failures and filtered-message-pump cleanup are outside this group. Hidden invalidated frames can retain old HWND allocation with zero rendered canvas.
producer_scope: Each final relevant producer bundle passes fmt, strict Clippy,125 workspace tests and x64/i686 builds. Producer checks are distinct from independent acceptance; preserved source-check failures remain linked by producer records.
